I take women’s rights seriously, so this is one of the first things I asked about while visiting Ghardaïa, Algeria  Now this is not necessarily for any reason. It has nothing to do with religion or location. The only thing it has to do with is that many communities that are small and follow old traditions typically give less rights and protections to women. However, I was pleasantly surprised that this is not the case in Ghardaia.   I really appreciate what I learned about  Mozabite communities, giving women in their own committees and ability to make decisions for themselves. When it comes to dress, extra protections, to feel safe and comfortable in their marriages, and the community standing in solidarity with its women. How safe is Algeria? 🇩🇿 Algeria might have the best police in the world. My friend, who is also a foreigner, had her phone taken, so we went to the police station to file a report. They guaranteed us that they would find the phone within a day and return it. I didn’t believe them. Within one day they called us and told us they got the phone. 😮 I’ve never experienced safety like this in any other country in the world. 👏 #algeria #algiers #travelvlog #travelalgeria #solotravel

Historically, the #Karakou is a traditional Algerian velvet jacket originating in Algiers, particularly the Casbah, known for its intricate gold embroidery. 🇩🇿 Recognised as part of Algeria’s rich traditional craftsmanship, it reflects the country’s living cultural heritage. Today, designers and couturiers such as Menouba, Eddine Belmahdi and ZK Haute Couture continue to celebrate and reinterpret this iconic garment, preserving its elegance while bringing it into modern fashion. #fyp #algeria #schiaparelliparis #viral
